title: CMA secures important changes from Google to tackle fake reviews - GOV.UK

facts.fact: Google's undertakings require it to report to the CMA over a 3-year period to show it is complying with them.
facts.quote: To ensure Google is complying with the undertakings it has signed, the firm will report to the CMA over a 3-year period.

facts.fact: Under Google's undertakings, businesses found to be boosting star ratings with fake reviews have their review function deactivated, and those that repeatedly do so have all their reviews deleted for 6 months or more.
facts.quote: Those firms that repeatedly engage in fake review activity will have all their reviews deleted for 6 months or more.

facts.fact: The CMA estimated that as much as £23 billion of UK consumer spending is potentially influenced by online reviews annually.
facts.quote: estimated that as much as £23 billion of UK consumer spending is potentially influenced by online reviews annually

facts.fact: According to research cited by the CMA from Which?, 89% of consumers use online customer reviews when researching a product or service.
facts.quote: research has shown that 89% of consumers use online customer reviews when researching a product or service

facts.fact: Under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, the CMA will be able to fine firms that break consumer law up to 10% of their global turnover.
facts.quote: The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 will empower the CMA to fine firms that break the law up to 10% of their global turnover.

facts.fact: The CMA's strengthened consumer powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 were expected to come into force in April 2025.
facts.quote: When this comes into force (expected in April 2025)

facts.fact: The CMA press release announcing Google's fake review undertakings was published on 24 January 2025.
